name: Tali Allen
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember pretending to enjoy a mystery to impress somebody.” On Thursday, near the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, Tali prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I am giving back a detective novel I stole to impress a girl who hated mysteries.
appearance: Tali is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Usually dressed in an unlined tan jacket with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case, Tali looks toward the door whenever a name is called when listening.
personality: Tali takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Tali can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To return the detective novel in person.
family: Vera Hardy is Tali’s half-sibling. Tali is free to hang up first. Vera makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A wall of birthdays*, Vera says, “My landlord says the wall belongs to him. I'd like him to meet the grandmother who owns the pencil.”
connections: Devin Bruno. They look through remembered nicknames for the first owner of a borrowed mystery. Also in the story is Elaine Aguilar (fellow borrower).
